METHODS OF TEST FOR POLYVINYL CHLORIDE BOOTS
PART 7 FLEXING TO CUT GROWTH TEST - RESISTANCE SOLING MATERIAL FOR

Prescribes the method for determining the resistance of soling material of Polyvinyl I. scope;hloride boots when subjected to repeated ,flexing or bending under specific conditions and for tnown period on flexing machine ( Satra ROSS type ). 2. Terminology - For the purpose of this standard, `Glossary of footwear terms' shall apply. the definitions given in IS : 2060-1967

3. Principle - This test gives a measure of the resistance of soling material to cracking resulting from flexing in wear. The material is repeatedly flexed through 90` over a mandrel after a small The rate of growth of this cut is a measure of cut has been made right through it with a chisel, the tendency of the material to crack. 4, Apparatus 0.1 Flexing machine ( Satra Ross type ) having a flexing mechanism as shown in Fig. 1A and 1 B .

4.1.1 The test piece A is inserted against the end stop of the flexing arm 8 and held by the clamp C in which length JK is 50 f 5 mm. The other end of the test piece is not clamped but moves in and out between rollers 0, E and F as the test piece is flexed. The flexing takes place round mandrel H which has a radius of curvature of 5.0 f 0.3 mm. 4.1.2 The distance in plan between the vertical tangent to this mandrel through point G and the adjacent edge J of clamp C is 11 #O f 0'5 mm. The chisel cut previously made in the test piece, is positioned vertically above the edge of the mandrel when the test piece is in the unflexed position, that is, at point G in Fig. 1,
4 1 3 The tops of rollers E and F and mandrel H are in the same horizontal plane and roller D is vertically above roller E. Except for this, the dimensions and positions of rollers 0, E and F are not critical. A suitable diameter for rollers D and E is 25 mm and for roller F is 10 mm or 15 mm. A suitable distance in plan between the centres of rollers D and E and the centre of curvature of mandrel H is 30 mm, and between the centres of rollers D and E and the centre of roller F is 25 mm or 30 mm, The vertical position of roller D is adjustable so that the gap between this and A locking mechanism is provided to roller E can accommodate test pieces of various thicknesses. ensure that the gap cannot change during a test. 4.1.4 Roller F has two adjustable collars. Their purpose is to help to position the unclamped end of the test piece during insertion in the apparatus, so that test piece is at right-angles to the flexing mandrel in plan, and to guide it in that position during flexing. The difference between the internal and external diameter of each collar should be about 10 mm. For the standard test piece, the distance between the collars should be from 25.5 mm to 26.0 mm. 4.1.5 The frequency of flexing shall be 1.0 f 0.1 Hz. at 5 f 2�C. The driving motor of the

Preparation

of Test Pieces

5.1 The standard test piece is 25 mm wide by 250 mm long, and the standard thicknesses are 3 to 6, 5 to 7, 7 to 10 and 15.0 mm, Test three pieces from the soling material. Remove any pattern and reduce the thickness of the test pieces to a standard thickness by cutting and very light Pierce each test piece approximately 60 mm from one end buffing of both sides of the test piece. The chisel so that the length of the cut is symmetrical across the centre line of the test piece. shall penetrate right through the test piece and protrude 15 mm on the other side, except for test pieces 10 0 and 15'0 mm thick, when a depth of cut of 7.5 mm is allowable. An adjustable collar may be fitted to the chisel shank to control the penetration distance of the chisel. 6. Conditioning and Temperature of Test

6.1 Condition the test piece for 24 h at 27 & 2�C and 65 f 5 percent relative humidity [ see IS : 196-1966 `Atmospheric condition of temperature ( revised )' 1. ( The testing is to be carried out at a temperature of - 5 f 2"C, if the note under 4 2 is made applicable. ) The test shall not normally be carried out in less than 7 days after moulding. 7 Procedure check of the rate of flexing of the machine to ensure that it runs at the

7 1 Make preliminary correct speed.

7.2 Measure and record the initial length of the cut in each test piece to an accuracy of 0 3 mm. This may most conveniently be done by using a magnifying eyepiece and scale with the test piece bent through 45" round a 15 mm diameter mandrel. 3

IS : 12240 ( Part 7) - 1988 7.3 Turn the drive wheel of the flexing machine manually until the flexing arm B is horizontal. Raise the top roller D by slackening the knurled knobs which secures the top frame of the machine. Slacken each clamping plate C. Insert each test piece, wearing surface uppermost, from the back of the machine ( the flexing arm B is assumed to be at the front ) so that it passes between rollers D and E, and then between the clamp C and flexing arm B and abuts against the end stop of 8. Roller F and the flexing arm B are both recessed so as to assist in positioning the strip test pieces. Clamp C holds two test pieces, one on each side of the centre screw which fixes it to arm B. Check that the cut in each test piece is vertically above the edge of mandrel G, then tighten clamp C, making sure that it is parallel to the edge of the flexing arm. Should only one test piece be held in a particular clamp, insert a small piece of the same material in the recess on the other side of the clamp so that the surface of the clamp remains parallel to the surface of the flexing area when it is tightened. Screw down roller D so that it just touches, but does not grip, the test piece. Look this roller by tightening the wing-nut, which is on the same screw thread, against the frame of the machine.
Test piece is mounted, since the test pieces will immediately, Note - Flexing should commence altieys be at a higher running temperature then the cabinet because of heating by flexing, and it has been found better for the test piece to cool to this running temperature during the initial Part of this test than for it to start colder and then warm up.

7.4 After the flexing has been started, inspect the test pieces at frequent intervals ( say every hour initially ) for evidence of any increase in length of the initial cut or of new cracks forming. 7.5 To do this, remove all the test pieces from the cabinet, measure bending through 45" round a 16 mm mandrel, and then replace all the under the initial loading procedure. 7.8 If for any reason flexing is discontinued, should be continued until either: a) the initial cut has increased b) until the test pieces have flexed increasing in length by 6 mm. remove the the crack lengths after test pieces as described Flexing

test pieces from the machine&

by 6 mm or more, or for the specified number of cycles without the initial cut

7.7 In case (a), it is usually impossible to observe the number of flexes when the amount of cut growth is exactly 6 mm but it should be possible to make observations when it is a little less and a little more than this value. The number of flexes for 6 mm growth may then be obtained by interpolation either graphically or arithmetically. 7.7.1 In case (b), measure the length calculate the amount of cut growth, 8. Expression of Results of the crack after the specified number of cycles and

8.1 If the end point of the test is reached before the specified number of cycles, express the result as the number of cycles for the cut to increase in length by 6 mm, 8.2 If the test reached the specified number of cycles ( that is, the cut did not increase in length by 6 mm after this number of flexes ), express the result as the increase in cut length after the specified number of cycles. Record the temperature of test.
